title: Reinforcement Learning Improves Traversal of Parametric Knowledge in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2511.05933v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is often credited with improving reasoning at the expense of factual knowledge. We instead find that reasoning models outperform their instruction-tuned versions on factual recall by accessing existing parametric knowledge more effectively. Across five model families, structured prompting, which explicitly guides models through hierarchical traversal, recovers most of this gap, suggesting that much of the missing knowledge is latent rather than absent. Controlled RL experiments further support this: training on unseen, non-extractable facts improves recall of held-out, frequent but previously inaccessible facts, ruling out simple data exposure. Decomposing the training objective further attributes this gain to iterated on-policy exploration. translated_title: 强化学习改进大语言模型对参数化知识的遍历
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）通常被认为是以牺牲事实知识为代价来提升推理能力。我们反而发现，推理模型在事实回忆方面优于其指令微调版本，因为它们能够更有效地访问已有的参数化知识。在五个模型家族中，通过显式引导模型进行层级遍历的结构化提示方法能够弥合这一差距的大部分，这表明许多缺失的知识是潜在的而非不存在的。受控的强化学习实验进一步支持了这一点：在未见过的、不可直接提取的事实上进行训练，可以提升对保留的、频繁但此前无法访问的事实的回忆能力，从而排除了单纯数据暴露的解释。对训练目标的进一步分解将这一提升归因于迭代的同策略（on-policy）探索。同样的机制在行为层面和模型内部均有所体现：推理优势随检索深度增加而增长，同时逐层分析发现了相似的事实表征……
tldr: 本研究通过受控强化学习实验证明，推理模型的事实召回优势源于更有效地遍历已有参数化知识而非新增知识，其中迭代式的同策略探索是提升知识访问能力的关键机制。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates through controlled RL experiments that reasoning models' advantage in factual recall stems from more effectively traversing existing parametric knowledge rather than acquiring new knowledge, with iterated on-policy exploration identified as the key mechanism.
